subproblems.title: Upper bound M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) for every W (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3), ≤ half)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set (not assumed open). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n): M ⊆ U Borel and countably n-rectifiable; θ : ℝ^P → ℕ Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (continuous linear functionals on the space E of n-covectors on ℝ^P) a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are an approximate tangent space Q of M at x and an orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n spanning Q with ξ(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α ∈ E, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all α ∈ E. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) be represented by R: T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), the smooth compactly supported n-forms with tsupport ω ⊆ U. Put μ_R := θ Hⁿ⌞M, i.e. the contract's R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ. Then M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) for every set W ⊆ ℝ^P (not assumed open or measurable), where M_W(T) := sup{ofReal(T(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} ∈ [0, ∞] (SimonGMT massOn; the zero form is admissible) and |α| := (Σ_{1≤i_1<⋯<i_n≤P} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors (covectorEuclideanNorm; Simon 6.1.15, 6.2.5).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), T.massOn W ≤ R.measure W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), the inequality M_W(T) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ; Simon states 3.2(3) without proof, and the argument is property (a) of Remark 2.6 (lines 243–263). Provenance (not a proof step): extracted from step 4, and the parts of steps 1–3 it uses, of the proof supplied for the parent theorem cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, here written for arbitrary U and W; the argument below is self-contained. Notation. E := Covector(ℝ^P, n), the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (a finite-dimensional real vector space); e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis; I ranges over the strictly increasing maps {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}), and |α| := (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, and μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ_R(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for every Borel set B, μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and μ_R (like every measure) is monotone on arbitrary sets. For an E-valued map g we write ξ(g) for the real function x ↦ ξ(x)(g(x)).
1. (Algebra.) Let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P and α ∈ E. If n = 0, τ is the empty family, the only index tuple I is the empty one (vacuously strictly increasing), and |α| = |α(∅)| = |α(τ)|. Let n ≥ 1; an orthonormal family is linearly independent, so n ≤ P. Let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, so τ_i = Σ_k A_{ik} e_k, and let A_I := (A_{i,I(j)})_{i,j} be the n×n submatrix with columns I. By multilinearity, α(τ) = Σ_k (Π_i A_{i,k(i)}) α(e_{k(1)}, …, e_{k(n)}), the sum over all maps k : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}. Terms with k not injective vanish because α is alternating; every injective k is uniquely k = I∘σ with I strictly increasing and σ a permutation of {1, …, n}, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ) α(e_I). Grouping the terms, (a) α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i A_{i,I(σ(i))} = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I). By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, |α(τ)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ), where (AAᵀ)_{ij} = Σ_k ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_{ij}; so Σ_I det(A_I)² = 1 and (b) |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E.
2. (A.e. dual bound for ξ.) By the field `orients` of R, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf(ξ(x), Q), i.e. an orthonormal τ : {1, …, n} → ℝ^P with ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α ∈ E or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α ∈ E. By step 1(b), for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x: |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. (The approximate-tangent-space clause is not used. If n > P, no orthonormal n-family exists, so this a.e. statement forces Hⁿ(M) = 0 and all integrals below vanish; the argument covers this case unchanged.)
3. (Reduction to one admissible form.) By definition M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over the admissible ω, i.e. ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (smooth, compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. So it suffices to prove ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ_R(W) for one fixed admissible ω. Put S := tsupport ω; S is closed (hence Borel) and compact, S ⊆ U and S ⊆ W.
4. (Finiteness.) Since S is a compact subset of U, the field `locallyIntegrable_mult` of R gives μ_R(S) = ∫⁻_{M∩S} θ dHⁿ < ∞. Hence the function θ·1_S is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable and ∫ θ 1_S d(Hⁿ⌞M) = μ_R(S).toReal.
5. (Pointwise bound.) Let f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)). Then f is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (θ is Borel, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, ω is continuous, and the evaluation (η, α) ↦ η(α) is continuous). For Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x: if x ∈ S, then |f(x)| ≤ θ(x)|ω(x)| ≤ θ(x) by step 2 and |ω| ≤ 1; if x ∉ S, then ω(x) = 0, hence ξ(x)(ω(x)) = 0 by linearity of ξ(x) and f(x) = 0. Thus |f| ≤ θ 1_S, and in particular f ≤ θ 1_S, Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.
6. (Integral bound.) By steps 4–5, f is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable. By R.Represents T and the definition of R.action, T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞M) ≤ ∫ θ 1_S d(Hⁿ⌞M) = μ_R(S).toReal by monotonicity of the integral. Therefore ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ ofReal(μ_R(S).toReal) = μ_R(S) (as μ_R(S) < ∞) ≤ μ_R(W), the last inequality by monotonicity of the measure μ_R, since S ⊆ W; no measurability of W is needed.
7. (Conclusion.) Taking the supremum over all admissible ω gives M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W). Neither openness of U nor openness or measurability of W was used. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cauchy–Binet: for an orthonormal n-family τ in ℝ^P, α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I) and Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1, so |α(τ)| ≤ |α|; hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x by `orients`.
Fix an admissible ω with S := tsupport ω ⊆ W: S is compact in U, so μ_R(S) = ∫_{M∩S} θ dHⁿ < ∞, and θ·ξ(ω) ≤ θ·1_S Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (|ω| ≤ 1, ω = 0 off S).
T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ ≤ μ_R(S).toReal, so ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ μ_R(S) ≤ μ_R(W) by monotonicity; take the supremum over admissible ω.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–768), the inequality ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ ≤ M_W(T) for open W; Simon states 3.2(3) without proof, and the argument is the one indicated by property (b) of Remark 2.6 (lines 243–263) together with 2.7–2.8 (lines 265–283). Provenance (not a proof step): extracted from steps 1–3 and 5–11 of the proof supplied for the parent theorem cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, with the details filled in; the argument below is self-contained. Throughout, U and W are open. Notation. E := Covector(ℝ^P, n), the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ (a finite-dimensional real vector space); e_1, …, e_P is the standard basis; I ranges over the strictly increasing maps {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}, e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}), and |α| := (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, and μ_R = R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ_R(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for every Borel set B, μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and μ_R (like every measure) is monotone on arbitrary sets. For an E-valued map g we write ξ(g) for the real function x ↦ ξ(x)(g(x)).
1. (Algebra.) Let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P and α ∈ E. If n = 0, τ is the empty family, the only index tuple I is the empty one (vacuously strictly increasing), and |α| = |α(∅)| = |α(τ)|. Let n ≥ 1; an orthonormal family is linearly independent, so n ≤ P. Let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, so τ_i = Σ_k A_{ik} e_k, and let A_I := (A_{i,I(j)})_{i,j} be the n×n submatrix with columns I. By multilinearity, α(τ) = Σ_k (Π_i A_{i,k(i)}) α(e_{k(1)}, …, e_{k(n)}), the sum over all maps k : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P}. Terms with k not injective vanish because α is alternating; every injective k is uniquely k = I∘σ with I strictly increasing and σ a permutation of {1, …, n}, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ) α(e_I). Grouping the terms, (a) α(τ) = Σ_I α(e_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i A_{i,I(σ(i))} = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I). By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, |α(τ)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ), where (AAᵀ)_{ij} = Σ_k ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩⟨τ_j, e_k⟩ = ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = δ_{ij}; so Σ_I det(A_I)² = 1 and (b) |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. Next define ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) on E. It is an inner product whose norm is |·|: it is bilinear, symmetric and ⟨α, α⟩_E = |α|² ≥ 0, and if α(e_I) = 0 for every I then α(e_k) = 0 for every k : {1, …, n} → {1, …, P} (for k not injective by the alternating property, for k = I∘σ because α(e_k) = sgn(σ) α(e_I)), so α = 0 by multilinearity. In particular |·| is a norm on E. Define α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}; it is multilinear and alternating in (v_1, …, v_n) (the v_j are the columns), hence α_τ ∈ E, and α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I). Hence (c) ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = Σ_I α(e_I) det(A_I) = α(τ) for every α ∈ E by (a), |α_τ|² = Σ_I det(A_I)² = 1, and α_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j} = 1. (For n = 0, α_τ is the constant covector 1 and (c) holds trivially.)
2. (Dual field.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism of ⟨·,·⟩_E, i.e. ⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α) for all α ∈ E and η ∈ E*; it exists, is unique and is a continuous linear map because E is finite-dimensional and ⟨·,·⟩_E is an inner product. Put β := J ∘ ξ : ℝ^P → E. Since ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, both ξ and β are μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable. By the field `orients`, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, hence for μ_R-a.e. x, there are s ∈ {1, −1} and an orthonormal τ with ξ(x)(α) = s·α(τ) for all α ∈ E. For such x, step 1 gives: (i) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E; (ii) β(x) = s·α_τ, since ⟨α, s α_τ⟩_E = s α(τ) = ξ(x)(α) for every α, so |β(x)| = 1; (iii) ξ(x)(β(x)) = s·(s α_τ)(τ) = s² α_τ(τ) = 1. (If n > P, no orthonormal n-family exists, so `orients` forces Hⁿ(M) = 0, hence μ_R = 0 and the theorem is trivial; the argument below covers this case anyway.)
3. (Local finiteness and the integral formula.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field `locallyIntegrable_mult`. Let g : ℝ^P → E be continuous with compact support L := tsupport g ⊆ U. Then ξ(g) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable (evaluation is continuous), and μ_R-a.e. |ξ(x)(g(x))| ≤ |g(x)| ≤ C·1_L(x) with C := sup_x |g(x)| < ∞, by (i) and since g = 0 off L; as μ_R(L) < ∞, ξ(g) is μ_R-integrable. If moreover g = ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then by R.Represents T, the definition of R.action, and ∫ h d(ν.withDensity θ) = ∫ θ h dν for the Borel, finite-valued density θ: T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_R.
4. (Reduction to compact sets.) Put V := U ∩ W, an open set. Since U is open, ℝ^P∖U is Borel and μ_R(ℝ^P∖U) = ∫⁻_{M∖U} θ dHⁿ = 0 because M ⊆ U; as W is Borel, μ_R(W) = μ_R(W ∩ U) + μ_R(W∖U) = μ_R(V). If V = ∅, then μ_R(W) = 0 ≤ M_W(T). Otherwise, for i ≥ 1 let K_i := {x : |x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P, and K_i := {x : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P∖V) ≥ 1/i} if V ≠ ℝ^P. Each K_i is closed and bounded, hence compact; K_i ⊆ V (points outside V have distance 0 to ℝ^P∖V); K_i ⊆ K_{i+1}; and ⋃_i K_i = V, because each x ∈ V has dist(x, ℝ^P∖V) > 0 (the complement is closed). By continuity from below, μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). Hence it suffices to prove (★) μ_R(K) ≤ M_W(T) for every compact K ⊆ V; and since μ_R(K) < ∞ by step 3 (K ⊆ U), it suffices to prove μ_R(K) ≤ M_W(T) + 4η for every real η > 0. Fix such K and η. If μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove, so assume μ_R(K) > 0; in particular K ≠ ∅.
5. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V (any δ > 0 if V = ℝ^P; otherwise 2δ < dist(K, ℝ^P∖V), which is positive because K is compact, ℝ^P∖V is closed, and they are disjoint). For 0 < s ≤ δ let O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}; it is open, K ⊆ O_s ⊆ D := {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ}, and D is closed and bounded, hence a compact subset of V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_s) ≤ μ_R(D) < ∞ by step 3. Since K is closed, the decreasing sets O_{δ/j} (j ≥ 1) have intersection {x : dist(x, K) = 0} = K, so by continuity from above μ_R(O_{δ/j}) → μ_R(K). Fix s := δ/j with μ_R(O_s) < μ_R(K) + η and put O := O_s. Then O is open, K ⊆ O ⊆ V, μ_R(O) < ∞, and μ_R(O∖K) = μ_R(O) − μ_R(K) < η.
6. (Lusin.) Since β is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a Borel map β̃ : ℝ^P → E with β = β̃ μ_R-a.e.; choose a Borel μ_R-null set N containing {β ≠ β̃} and the μ_R-null set of points where (i)–(iii) of step 2 fail (every null set is contained in a Borel null set). Put A := K∖N, a Borel set with μ_R(A) = μ_R(K) < ∞. The restriction ν := μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P, hence closed-inner-regular on Borel sets. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean, exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable), applied to each of the m := dim E coordinates of β̃ in a basis of E with tolerance η/m and intersecting the m closed sets obtained (if m = 0, β̃ = 0 and closed inner regularity of ν alone gives the set), there is a closed set K' ⊆ A with ν(A∖K') < η and β̃|K' continuous. K' is compact, being closed and contained in K. Since K' ∩ N = ∅, β = β̃ on K', so β|K' is continuous, and at every x ∈ K': |β(x)| = 1, ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1, and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α ∈ E. Moreover μ_R(K∖K') ≤ μ_R(A∖K') + μ_R(N) = ν(A∖K') < η.
7. (Continuous extension, truncation and cut-off.) By Tietze's extension theorem applied to the coordinates of β|K' in a basis of E (K' is closed), there is a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E with g_0 = β on K'. Let r : E → E be r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1 and r(α) := α/|α| if |α| ≥ 1; the two formulas agree where |α| = 1 and both pieces are closed, so r is continuous, |r(α)| ≤ 1 for all α, and r(α) = α whenever |α| ≤ 1. Let χ(x) := max(0, 1 − 2 dist(x, K')/s) if K' ≠ ∅ and χ := 0 if K' = ∅. Then χ is continuous, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', and tsupport χ ⊆ L := {x : dist(x, K') ≤ s/2} if K' ≠ ∅ (L := ∅ otherwise); L ⊆ {x : dist(x, K) ≤ s/2} ⊆ O because K' ⊆ K, and L is closed and bounded, hence compact. Put g(x) := χ(x)·r(g_0(x)). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ L ⊆ O, |g(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and for x ∈ K' we have χ(x) = 1 and |g_0(x)| = |β(x)| = 1, so g(x) = r(β(x)) = β(x).
8. (Mollification.) If K' = ∅, then g = 0, and we put σ_0 := 1 and g_σ := 0 for every σ > 0; properties (a)–(d) below then hold trivially (with m(σ) = 0). Otherwise L ≠ ∅, and we choose σ_0 > 0 with {x : dist(x, L) ≤ σ_0} ⊆ O (any σ_0 > 0 if O = ℝ^P; otherwise 0 < σ_0 < dist(L, ℝ^P∖O), which is positive because L is compact and nonempty, ℝ^P∖O is closed, and L ∩ (ℝ^P∖O) = ∅). Let φ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞) be smooth, supported in the closed unit ball, with ∫ φ = 1, and φ_σ(y) := σ^{−P} φ(y/σ), which is smooth, ≥ 0, supported in the closed σ-ball, with ∫ φ_σ = 1. For 0 < σ ≤ σ_0 put g_σ(x) := ∫ g(x − y) φ_σ(y) dy = ∫ g(z) φ_σ(x − z) dz (E-valued Bochner integral, i.e. componentwise convolution in a basis of E). Then: (a) g_σ is C^∞, being the convolution of the continuous compactly supported g with the smooth compactly supported φ_σ; (b) if dist(x, L) > σ then x − y ∉ L for |y| ≤ σ, so g(x − y) φ_σ(y) = 0 for all y and g_σ(x) = 0; hence tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, L) ≤ σ}, a compact subset of O; (c) |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1, because |·| is a norm on E (step 1); (d) |g_σ(x) − g(x)| = |∫ (g(x − y) − g(x)) φ_σ(y) dy| ≤ m(σ) := sup{|g(a) − g(b)| : |a − b| ≤ σ}, and m(σ) → 0 as σ → 0 because g is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support). By (a)–(c), g_σ is an n-form in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (smooth, compact support, tsupport g_σ ⊆ O ⊆ V ⊆ U) which is admissible for M_W(T) (tsupport g_σ ⊆ O ⊆ V ⊆ W and |g_σ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x); hence ofReal(T(g_σ)) ≤ M_W(T).
9. (Estimate.) By step 3 (applied to g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and to g, whose support L ⊆ O ⊆ U is compact), T(g_σ) = ∫ ξ(g_σ) dμ_R and ξ(g) is μ_R-integrable. Since g_σ and g vanish off O, (i) and (d) give, μ_R-a.e., |ξ(x)(g_σ(x)) − ξ(x)(g(x))| = |ξ(x)(g_σ(x) − g(x))| ≤ |g_σ(x) − g(x)| ≤ m(σ)·1_O(x); hence T(g_σ) ≥ ∫ ξ(g) dμ_R − m(σ) μ_R(O). Split ℝ^P into K', O∖K' and ℝ^P∖O (K' ⊆ K ⊆ O, all Borel): on K', ξ(x)(g(x)) = ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 at every point (step 6); on O∖K', ξ(x)(g(x)) ≥ −|g(x)| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e. by (i); on ℝ^P∖O, g = 0 and ξ(g) = 0. Hence ∫ ξ(g) dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O∖K'). All these measures are finite, μ_R(K') = μ_R(K) − μ_R(K∖K') > μ_R(K) − η, and μ_R(O∖K') = μ_R(O∖K) + μ_R(K∖K') < 2η, so ∫ ξ(g) dμ_R > μ_R(K) − 3η. Choose σ ∈ (0, σ_0] with m(σ)·μ_R(O) < η (possible as μ_R(O) < ∞ and m(σ) → 0). Then T(g_σ) > μ_R(K) − 4η as real numbers, so μ_R(K) < T(g_σ) + 4η ≤ max(T(g_σ), 0) + 4η, i.e. μ_R(K) ≤ ofReal(T(g_σ)) + 4η ≤ M_W(T) + 4η in [0, ∞] by step 8.
10. (Conclusion.) Since η > 0 was arbitrary, μ_R(K) ≤ M_W(T) for every compact K ⊆ V, which is (★). By step 4, μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i) ≤ M_W(T), including the case μ_R(W) = ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: Algebra: the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E = Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) has norm |·|; for orthonormal τ, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet) and α_τ = det(⟨τ_i, ·⟩) satisfies ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ), |α_τ| = 1 = α_τ(τ).
Dual field β = J∘ξ (Riesz map of ⟨·,·⟩_E): μ_R-a.e. |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, |β| = 1, ξ(β) = 1; μ_R is finite on compact subsets of U and T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ_R.
Reduction: μ_R(W) = μ_R(U ∩ W) = sup over a compact exhaustion, so it suffices that μ_R(K) ≤ M_W(T) + 4η for compact K ⊆ U ∩ W and η > 0; choose open O = {dist(·, K) < s} ⊆ U ∩ W with μ_R(O∖K) < η.
Lusin gives compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K∖K') < η, β|K' continuous, |β| = 1 and ξ(β) = 1 on K'; Tietze, radial retraction and a cut-off give continuous g with compact support in O, |g| ≤ 1, g = β on K'.
Mollify: g_σ smooth, tsupport ⊆ O, |g_σ| ≤ 1, sup|g_σ − g| → 0, so g_σ is admissible and T(g_σ) ≥ ∫ ξ(g) dμ_R − sup|g_σ − g| μ_R(O) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η; let η → 0 and exhaust.
